title: Gemini 4 Argon now available on AI Gateway
description: Gemini 4 Argon from Google is now available on AI Gateway . Gemini 4 Argon is built for coding, agentic work, and complex reasoning. It has a 1M token context window, accepts text, image, PDF, and video input, and supports tool calling. On coding tasks, Gemini 4 Argon builds features, fixes bugs, and researches unfamiliar codebases, carrying longer tasks through multiple steps. The model also reads dense diagrams, spreadsheets, layout-heavy documents, and video, which suits tasks like a financial analysis spread across several spreadsheet tabs. Beyond code, it handles work in finance, health, and law, and hard problems in math and science. Gemini 4 Argon uses thinking levels ( low , medium , and high ) instead of thinking budgets. Call Gemini 4 Argon through the AI SDK , the Chat Completions , Responses , and Anthropic Messages APIs, or a coding agent connected to AI Gateway. Set the thinking level with reasoning in the AI SDK or reasoning_effort in Chat Completions, and see reasoning for the other controls. Use google/gemini-4-argon as the model name: To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup: Then select google/gemini-4-argon in the agent. See the coding agents guide for details. Try Gemini 4 Argon in the model playground . AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting , Zero Data Retention support , budgets for API keys , routing rules , and more. AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and does not charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests. You can view all language models available on AI Gateway. Read more

title: battledrones v14: Compass Rose, a four player map
description:
Release: battledrones v14: Compass Rose, a four player map

I added four player online mode to Battledrones - previous maps were limited to two.

Here's the initial prompt I used:

Add a new map for a four player battle - four way rotational symmetry, up to four AI players, works with the WebSocket non-audio based multiplayer mode so up to four human players can join (any spare slots use AI)

Claude Opus 5.5 added a new map called "Compass Rose" and modified the WebSockets multiplayer network code to support up to four players for that map, joining via share links or QR codes.

The new teams use robots themed in purple and green, joining the existing blue and red designs. You can preview those colors in the updated model browser.

Here's a replay link to watch a four way AI battle with the "Goliath Armada" mutator turned on, where each side starts with four giant Goliath mech units.

title: Quick Study
description:
Tool: Quick Study

Prompt to Claude Opus 5.5 High:

Build an artifact where you open a photo and it rapidly (in a few seconds) paints a version of that photo using a canvas element and simulated paintbrush

See also my previous experiment getting Claude Fable to simulate a watercolor illustration with P5.js.

Quick Study uses Sobel edge detection, with no external libraries beyond Google Fonts.

title: Introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro
description:
Introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro

Kimi K3.1 Pro landed on the Kimi API today - it's not yet open weights, but Moonshot promise "Full model weights will be released by Nov 4, 2026".

They're also offering a "Highspeed" version that's 2-3x faster, at twice the price (except for input token cache hits, which are priced the same).

The US dollar pricing is $2.00/million tokens for input and $10/million for output - the same as GPT-6.1 Sol and half the price of Claude Opus 5.5.

Moonshot's own benchmarks show Kimi as approximately level with Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra - beating them on a few benchmarks, coming close on others.

Artificial Analysis scored Kimi at 55 - ahead of Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-6 Astra, and Gemini 4 Argon (all at 53) and behind only Claude Opus 5.5 (58).

This is the first time a (soon-to-be) open weight model has scored this highly against the frontier.

I tried it out via the Moonshot API using the llm openai endpoint command I added to LLM 0.32 back in August:

llm openai endpoint \ https://api.moonshot.ai/v1 \ --key kimi \ -m kimi-k3.1-pro \ "Generate an SVG of a pelican riding a bicycle" \ --responses \ -o reasoning_effort low \ > kimi-k3.1-pro-pelican-low.stdout.txt \ 2> kimi-k3.1-pro-pelican-low.stderr.txt

llm openai endpoint can run prompts against any OpenAI-compatible endpoint but doesn't log the results, hence the extra options to save stdout and stderr (the reasoning trace).

Here are the pelicans I got for Kimi K3.1 Pro on the three reasoning levels it supports - low, medium, and max. This is max:

For comparison, I ran fresh pelicans against Kimi K3 on those three reasoning levels.

Via Hacker News

title: Donating Agent Skills to the Agentic AI Foundation
description:
Donating Agent Skills to the Agentic AI Foundation

News today from Anthropic:

We’re committed to keeping Agent Skills open, community-driven, and vendor-neutral. Today, we are donating the standard to the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) under the Linux Foundation, which we co-founded with Block and OpenAI last year, and to which we donated the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

I'm pleased to note I called this one last December, when Anthropic first declared skills to be an "open standard":

I wouldn't be surprised to see this end up in the AAIF, recently the new home of the MCP specification.

Fun side note: since my blog content is available to Claude via the datasette-mcp plugin I found that post by prompting Claude to "Use simonwillison.net MCP to find if I ever talked about how I want skills to be donated to a standards body".

Tags: standards, ai, generative-ai, llms, anthropic, model-context-protocol, skills
